clue.text: Celebratory meal created by 25

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun: the thing that the sculptor at 25 across made

parts.note: a gala is a celebratory occasion or festivity
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain

explanation.surface: A festive dinner has been laid on by somebody referred to only as 25.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on another light: 25 across is PYGMALION, the sculptor of Greek myth whose statue came to life.
explanation.definitionFit: In the myth, the ivory statue carved by the sculptor Pygmalion and brought to life bears this name.

clue.text: Giggler in the sand going off at high speed

indicators.note: to go off is to explode or go wrong, so the four words before it are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Somebody tittering on the beach suddenly shoots away very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for extreme speed, as if moving like a lubricated thunderbolt.

clue.text: See 1
Recipient of letter from bird (American)

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
US is short for United States, hence American

explanation.surface: Someone receives a letter sent by an American bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' here is a New Testament epistle, the Epistle of Paul to Titus.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul addressed one of his New Testament epistles to this companion and church leader.

clue.text: Silver was sorry to be having a grouch

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
grieved means felt sorrow

explanation.surface: Someone called Silver felt regret while nursing a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resentful because one feels wronged is the same as nursing a grouch or grievance.

clue.text: Many more than one over the limit in 2010?

definitions.text: Many more than one over the limit
definitions.meaning: 'one over the ...' is British slang for being slightly drunk, so this time is well past that limit
read on a 24-hour clock, 20:10 is a time of evening rather than a year

explanation.walkthrough: '2010' looks like a year; read as 20:10 on a 24-hour clock it is a time. 'One over the eight' is a British phrase for a drink too many.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings name the clock time 20:10, which is also comfortably more than 'one over the eight'.

clue.text: 8's instincts are to be scared

parts.note: 8 down is TIMOTHY, whose usual short form is Tim
the id is the instinctive part of the psyche in Freudian theory

explanation.surface: Somebody's natural impulses tell them to be afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being timid means being easily frightened, so it stands for being inclined to be scared.

clue.text: Undiluted science fiction too elevated? One could be 1 down with it

definitions.text: One could be 1 down with it

parts.note: a neat drink is one taken without water

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word up the grid means writing it from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Pure science fiction may be a little too lofty for its readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is GREASED: the oil rendered from cattle feet is used to grease leather.
explanation.definitionFit: This oil made from cattle feet is used to grease and soften leather, so something could be greased with it.

clue.text: Fairy accepting signal, say

indicators.note: 'say' asks for a word spoken, so the device described is pronounced rather than written

parts.note: a television aerial is the thing that picks up a broadcast signal

explanation.surface: A fairy is taking in some kind of signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The airy spirit who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest is a sprite or fairy.

clue.text: Recipient of letter: solver's to skip up first

indicators.note: first places the upturned word ahead of the possessive that precedes it in the clue
in a down clue, going up means writing the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to omit something is to skip it
thy is the archaic form of your, the solver's

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a letter tells the solver that their own part should be skipped first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is a New Testament epistle: Paul wrote two to Timothy.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul addressed two New Testament epistles to this young follower.

clue.text: See 5
Amusing my editor in place of exercise

indicators.note: an editor rearranges copy, so the two words before it are reordered

explanation.surface: An entertaining editor of mine works in a sports hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Editor' is a loose anagram signal: an editor reworks what is written.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall equipped for physical training is the classic place where people exercise.

clue.text: Day is provided when retiring editor has had enough

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday
taken as written

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for provided is written backwards

parts.note: if means provided that

explanation.surface: The day arrives when an editor stepping down has had his fill.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sated or full is to have eaten as much as one wants, much like having had enough.

clue.text: Having no children touched off divorce

parts.note: s.p. is the genealogists' abbreviation for sine prole, Latin for without issue
to touch off a fire or fuse is to light it, giving lit

explanation.surface: Being childless set off the couple's divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: A separation of a married couple, especially a break-up, is a common synonym for divorce.

clue.text: Finished around river, out of water

indicators.note: around says the word for finished goes around the river's letter

parts.note: died means came to an end, finished

explanation.surface: Done with being near the river, something emerges dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dehydrated or desiccated has had its water removed, so it is out of water.

clue.text: When Grahame was a child and made off in wagons

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for wagons

parts.note: drays are low heavy carts used by brewers

indicators.note: off means awry or wrong, so the letters of made are rearranged

explanation.surface: In his childhood, Kenneth Grahame ran away in the carts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' gives EAMD. Kenneth Grahame, author of The Wind in the Willows, wrote a book of childhood memories under this title.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1898 book by Kenneth Grahame recalls the days of his boyhood.

clue.text: Saviour working for liberty first and last in more ways than one

indicators.note: working here means operating in a new arrangement, so the letters of Saviour are reworked
first and last picks the opening and closing letters of the word liberty

explanation.surface: The Saviour campaigns for freedom from start to finish in several ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in differing manners means doing it in more ways than one.

clue.text: Suggestion about benefit once topped

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the dole is British state unemployment benefit

indicators.note: topped means its top cut off, and in a down clue the top is the first letter

explanation.surface: A hint that unemployment pay was once stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent or air that brings something to mind is a suggestion of it.

clue.text: I wander around idly and, come Easter, run off

indicators.note: off means gone awry, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to strolling about aimlessly and, when Easter arrives, running away.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroller or idler is one who wanders about at a leisurely pace, as the clue's 'I' does.

clue.text: Guardian leader, one in black and white, not about to change

indicators.note: in puts the newspaper's letter and the leader inside the word for black and white

parts.note: pied means patched in two colours, typically black and white
G is the newspaper's familiar initial
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: The Guardian's editor, a magpie of a figure, refuses to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubborn person is obstinate and will not change their mind.

clue.text: The hat I said I'd eat? It isn't true

definitions.text: The hat I said I'd eat?
definitions.meaning: a felt hat with a flat crown, also a meat pie one might eat, recalling 'I'll eat my hat'
rhyming slang, shortened to porky, for a lie

explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll eat my hat' is a vow made when sure of something. Rhyming slang 'porky pies' means lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a flat-crowned hat, a pastry one eats, and in rhyming slang a lie.

clue.text: See 24
Man retaining old signaller's letter on line causes computer problem

indicators.note: on means placed after, as in a down clue one piece sits upon the next
retaining means holding, so the pronoun holds the signal letter inside it

parts.note: he is the male pronoun, standing for a man
ack was the First World War signallers' word for the letter A
Ry is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A man holding an old signal letter on the line is causing trouble with the computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacking is breaking into computer systems, a security problem for the machine.

clue.text: Flower from space, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: room means space

explanation.surface: A bloom grows out of empty space, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is not a bloom but something that flows: watery discharge from eyes or nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A watery discharge from the eyes or nose is something that flows.

clue.text: Top bird, perhaps, not top dog

indicators.note: not top means without its first letter, the top in a down clue

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

explanation.surface: The best of birds maybe, but no top dog.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, two under par beats a birdie, so this could be called a top bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey is often called the king of birds, and in golf it outranks a birdie.

clue.text: Epstein left centre awfully cross

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for centre

explanation.surface: Epstein left the middle feeling terribly angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen was thought the seat of bad temper, so this adjective means irritable or cross.

clue.text: Offshoot said to be blue

indicators.note: said asks for a word heard rather than written

parts.note: cyan is a greenish-blue colour

explanation.surface: A shoot from a plant is described as blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a young shoot used for grafting, or a descendant of a family.

clue.text: Daughter taken off, girl following: there are the bare facts

indicators.note: following places the girl's name after the scrambled letters
off means awry, so D and the letters of taken are rearranged

parts.note: Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The daughter has been taken away and a girl comes after: those are the unvarnished facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns D plus TAKEN into NAKEDT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the plain, unadorned truth, the bare facts with nothing hidden.

clue.text: Mother cat sounds 18 across in play

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: 18 across is PIGHEADED, and a pig is a pigheaded, obstinate person
ma is a familiar word for mother
the lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A mother cat makes stubborn noises during a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: The pig-sounding piece comes first despite the clue's order. The play is George Bernard Shaw's.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's 1913 comedy about the phonetics professor Henry Higgins bears this title.

clue.text: First year in university is performing extract from Mass

indicators.note: in puts the first year inside the university's name

parts.note: Keele is a university in Staffordshire, England
I is the Roman numeral one, so first
taken as written
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A first-year student at university is singing part of the Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First year' gives YR + I (year one), not the first letter of 'year'. KEELE is a university in Staffordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek plea, 'Lord, have mercy', is the opening section of the Mass.

clue.text: See 26
Getting on with tree at each end of library

parts.note: the elder is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

indicators.note: at each end of picks the opening and closing letters of library

explanation.surface: Someone is ageing alongside a tree at either end of the library.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, so it means advanced in years.
